doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: How jazz bands work: improvising as conversation
summary: Watkins compares playing with new musicians to conversation in a shared language, mentioning Mike Dubaniewicz and Orrin.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You’re playing tonight in this space. You’re playing with a musician you know really well. You’re also playing with musicians that I don’t think you’ve met. And this is not uncommon in the jazz world. Sometimes you get a gig then you get a band. But sometimes people are mystified by that. If someone who really likes jazz but doesn’t
understand how that’s possible, they say, “How does that work? How does jazz work like that?” Can you respond to them?

I think it’s good to compare it to the rules of a conversation and a language. As you and I are here having a conversation there’s a certain — we’ve learned, we met today and we’ve been learning to speak our entire lives this language, so that we can have a conversation. We can have a deep and meaningful conversation. And it’s like that in jazz. There’s nouns and verbs, pronouns. I mean there’s sentence structure. So there’s a language. It’s a broad language as is a spoken language. So that would be my best way to make a non-musician understand what’s going on there. There are things that are unsaid because we’ve all studied the language. And it has to start somewhere. My four year old son is learning to write his name you know, and that’s going to turn into him having hopefully one day a mastery of the language.
Has he learned the word “gig” yet?

Oh yeah. He knows when dad’s putting on his gig shoes. My father was a minister so it was church shoes. But for me it’s gig shoes. Yeah. But yeah so there’s a language there. Now when you have deeper relationships, you know, you can have more intimate, meaningful conversations. Of course I think the relationships are invaluable, when you talk about bands and regular relationships between people. Time counts for a lot you know. So I can have a great conversation with you but it’s not the same conversation that I could have with my mother, you know, or somebody that I know more. So yeah it’s interesting to see what’ll happen. I’ve got Mike — Mike and I were on the road, Mike Dubaniewicz and I were on the road with Maynard for years. And then Orrin and I are close. But the other guys, we’ll see how it goes. We’ll speak the language.
